content:
incident-bot: Pager: multiple hosts in ash-serving are reporting repeated GPU driver resets (Xid 13 / Xid 31) and ECC spikes. Auto-escalation to oncall.

SRE_Grace: paging in. seeing a cluster of resets on ash-rt-12/13/14. kernel logs show repeated 'Xid 13' and 'GPU ECC corrected' noise. :rotating_light:

infra_jordan: confirmed from node exporter metrics — GPU ECC errors spiked ~3m ago. telemetry shows memory errors correlate with driver restarts.

runtime_lee: what processes are on those nodes? heavy batched inference (gpt-like) ongoing overnight quotas. Could be sustained long seq lengths.

SRE_Grace: mostly customer workloads on Dedicated pools. A few autoscaled pods got rescheduled earlier.

support_ana: flagging downstream impact — a handful of customer requests retried, SLOs for latency breached on 2 tenants (cust-acm and cust-beta). Not yet widespread but trending.

eng_pm_sam: prioritizing. Are we in danger of node flapping / cascade? Any evictions observed?

infra_jordan: kube events show OOMKilled for a container on ash-rt-12 right before first reset. Then driver restart, kubelet restarted container, then another crash.

runtime_lee: paste of dmesg around the time:
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, PID=4231, GPU=0: XidError
[ 12345.679012] GPU ECC corrected errors: 1024
[ 12346.012345] nvidia: loading driver vXXX
```

SRE_Grace: plan proposals:
1) cordon ash-rt-12/13/14 to stop new pods landing
2) drain with --force for priority non-critical pods
3) restart node drivers and run memtest if flakiness persists
4) evict highest-memory pods first

ops-alex: +1, start cordon now. I'll run `kubectl cordon ash-rt-12` then `kubectl drain ash-rt-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` for immediate relief.

oncall-jules: I'll take over live coordination after handoff in 20m. current oncall is me on-call next shift, but handoff note: keep SLO comms to support.

SRE_Grace: ops-alex please do cordon/drain, and annotate nodes with `gpu:unstable` label so scheduler policy avoids them.

ops-alex: running commands:
```
kubectl cordon ash-rt-12
kubectl drain ash-rt-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl label node ash-rt-12 gpu=unstable --overwrite
```

ops-alex: draining ash-rt-12 succeeded, moving to ash-rt-13/14 sequentially to avoid capacity loss. :thumbsup:

support_ana: notified affected customers in staging and real-prod impact channels. We'll prepare an incident message if this expands.

runtime_lee: after draining, I'm restarting nvidia driver on ash-rt-12 to attempt a clean state. command: `systemctl restart nvidia-drm` then check `nvidia-smi -q` for ECC counters.

infra_jordan: note — if ECC corrected errors are increasing rapidly, hardware replacement may be needed. Let's collect GPU ECC logs and vendor support tickets.

SRE_Grace: execution notes: if restarts continue after driver reload, escalate to hardware team and schedule replacement. Meanwhile bump placement of critical pods to other AZs.

eng_pm_sam: customer impact summary so far: cust-acm saw ~2.3% request failures over last 10m, cust-beta ~1.1%. No total outage. We should prepare an internal severity-2 timeline.

incident-bot: automated snapshot: created incident-ash-2155006789, added runbook `gpu-driver-reset` and attached logs from ash-rt-12.

ops-alex: ash-rt-13 drain done. ash-rt-14 shows lower error rate, skipping for now. continuing monitoring.

runtime_lee: after driver restart on ash-rt-12, ECC counters decreased but we still see intermittent Xid 31s at low frequency. Running `nvidia-bug-report.sh` and collecting to /tmp/bugreports/ash-rt-12.tar.gz

SRE_Grace: OK. short-term mitigation: cordon+drain of affected nodes, relabel them unstable, shift traffic off Dedicated pool to burst capacity. Medium-term: schedule hardware diag and possible GPU replacement.

support_ana: drafting customer-facing blurb: "We're investigating GPU driver instability affecting a subset of Dedicated hosts in ash. Some requests may be retried or see increased latency. We're performing node evacuations and hardware diagnostics. We'll update within 30 minutes." any edits?

eng_pm_sam: add note about no data loss and that mitigation is in progress. good to include ETA for next update.

oncall-jules: I'm taking over for next 2 hours. SRE_Grace handing off: all active nodes labeled `gpu=unstable`, drains complete for 12/13, 14 monitored. Please escalate if restarts resume after driver restart.

SRE_Grace: handoff ack. I'll add runbook steps and links in the incident doc. thanks team.

ops-alex: following up: uploading `nvidia-bug-report` and kernel logs to incident doc: https://redwood-internal/incident/2155006789/logs

incident-bot: Incident status changed to 'Mitigating' by oncall-jules. Next automated check in 10 minutes.

support_ana: posted initial customer message in status page and pinned it to the incident.

eng_pm_sam: assigning postmortem owner: runtime_lee. Please capture timeline, root cause hypothesis (ECC/drivers/hardware), and next steps (hotfixes, hardware replacements, scheduler safeguards).

SRE_Grace: closing the live paging loop for now. keep monitoring and reopen if Xid spike > 5 per min across >2 nodes. :white_check_mark:
